column7: The one place a refusal's failed record write meets its policy: under a fail-closed log a FollowLog refusal settles as unavailable, so it is answered 503 or -32005 instead of as decided; a mistake lets a refusal go unrecorded quietly.
Records a stdio signing refusal through settle and answers -32005 when a fail-closed log could not record it, else the error's own code and words; the stdio twin of Refused::record.

Reads whether a request's id is present, absent or unreadable; only an id that is not present (absent or unreadable) lets the intake refusal answer when a fail-closed log could not record it, so a mistake would answer an unrecorded refusal as decided.

Builds what a signing refusal records (the outcome its error maps to, the target as named, the FollowLog policy, the kind its site implies); a mistake would record the wrong outcome or answer a fail-closed refusal as decided.
Records a /mcp signing refusal before answering it with HTTP 400, or 503 through record when a fail-closed log could not record it; a mistake would skip the record.
Records the early stdio malformed-nonce refusal through the shared writer before answering it, keeping its place ahead of every gate; a mistake would skip the record.
Builds the Refused the /mcp intake and early signing refusals are recorded under, with the caller identity Refused::of captures; a mistake records the refusal against the wrong principal.
Names the record principal every stdio record carries, keyed like any principal; a mistake records stdio refusals against the wrong principal.
Builds the audit who of an early stdio refusal made before the caller context exists, from the constant stdio parts; a mistake records the refusal against the wrong caller.
